conviction_note: Revenue very likely lands at or above the top of the $61-64B guide (four sell-side channel checks at $63.7-64.1B vs $63.3B consensus), but this name has sold its last three revenue-in-line-or-better prints on forward spend (-8.0% Q2-26, -8.6% Q1-26, -11.3% Q3-25, the last on exactly this first-look-at-next-year's-expenses call), and tonight carries the first 2027 capex/expense framing against a ~$193B capex bar that one bank (Evercore) expects to be exceeded; so the fundamental read is a small beat and the reaction lean is mildly negative, p_up 45 on an 8% absolute move (event-implied 6.3%, own median 8.55%). Sum of findings -1.2 vs scaled -0.8; the gap is that the scaled number lets the large-move uncertainty dominate.
bar: Revenue: company guide $61-64B (Q2-26 8-K exhibit 99.1, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001326801/000162828026050596/meta-06302026xexhibit991.htm) and consensus $63.24B Zacks (https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/buy-sell-hold-meta-stock-083700346.html, 2026-10-19) / $63.30B MarketBeat (https://www.gurufocus.com/news/9132560/us-stocks-rise-ahead-of-meta-platforms-meta-earnings-report-on-october-21-2026) - two agreeing sources. GAAP EPS bar is NOT usable: estimates range $3.79 (BofA, post $10B charge) to $6.54-$7.54 (pre-charge), per https://cmsinvestments.substack.com/p/meta-q3-preview-the-2027-capex-number. 2027 capex bar ~$193B consensus is single-source (same substack; BofA $205B, Evercore ~+$70B YoY), so the guidance finding is capped.
positioning_check: Short interest ~32.1M shares at the 2026-05-15 settlement, ~2.1 days to cover, ~1.3% of float, not crowded (https://equibles.com/stocks/meta/shortinterest; no October settlement found). Baseline 25-delta skew -2.0 vol points (calls slightly richer than puts), put/call OI 0.79, priced_direction_lean 'balanced'. Stock -3.98% 5d, -4.82% 20d, 8.9% under 52w high after a ~27% September run on the Muse launch; Investing.com 2026-10-19 describes defensive positioning/profit-taking into the print. Nothing here argues against a negative lean on squeeze grounds.

findings.finding: Four sell-side channel checks published in October put Q3 revenue above the $63.3B consensus and at/above the top of Meta's $61-64B guide: Deutsche Bank raised to $63.7B from $63.1B (checks show healthy core ads, higher engagement), BofA $63.8B, Bernstein $64.06B (~+25% YoY), Morgan Stanley checks 'solid'; one preview cites checks of +24.8% cc ad growth and ~350bp sequential CPM acceleration. Meta also landed near the top of its range the last two quarters.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2-26 revenue $60.8B (+28%) beat yet stock -7.95% on Q3 guide/costs; Q1-26 -8.55%, Q3-25 -11.33% on forward expense framing despite revenue beats. Revenue beats have not been paid for in 3 of the last 4 prints; Jan-26 +10.4% came with a strong Q1 guide.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: these are published sell-side notes, so the whisper is likely ~$64B rather than $63.3B. If fully priced the stock would not have drifted -4% in five sessions into the print; what is not priced is only the residual if revenue prints above $64B, the top of the guide.
findings.independence: Same direction from BofA estimate in https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/why-is-meta-platforms-stock-sliding-today-93CH-4957820 (2026-10-19) and the Bernstein/DB summary at https://www.tipranks.com/news/meta-q3-earnings-preview-what-bernstein-expects-from-meta-stock; all sell-side, not independent of each other.

findings.finding: Tonight is the first look at 2027 spend: Meta has given no 2027 capex number; previews put 2027 capex consensus at ~$193B (BofA $205B, Evercore ~+$70B YoY i.e. ~$200B+ on a $130-145B 2026 guide), Evercore's Mahaney expects capex and total expense targets ABOVE consensus and a cut to 2027 profit estimates, Morgan Stanley models D&A rising from ~$31.5B (2026) to ~$59B (2027), and Q2 free cash flow was only $784M.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The analogous call a year ago (Q3-25, 2025-10-29), when Meta said 2026 capex would be 'notably larger' and expenses would grow 'significantly faster', produced -11.33%; Q2-26 (raised expense guide) -7.95%; Q1-26 -8.55%. Forward-spend framing has been the line this stock trades on.
findings.why_not_priced: The consensus capex bar (~$193B) is below what two banks model ($200-205B), so a guide in line with those banks would still read as above consensus. If the market had fully absorbed a $200B+ number, the skew would lean to puts and the stock would not sit only 9% off its high after a 27% September rally; instead skew is -2 (calls bid). Capped because the capex bar is single-source.
findings.independence: Evercore/BofA 2027 EPS-pressure view also reported at https://finance.biggo.com/news/7704261d-f24f-48c4-b5be-014986e460d6 and BofA's warning on 2027 EPS in the TipRanks piece above; the reaction history is from the sealed baseline.

findings.finding: Q3 GAAP results will carry an ~$10B legal accrual for the 29-state youth-harm settlement (up to ~$18B over 10 years, ~$12.7B unconditional), which Meta said on 2026-08-26 is outside its $165-169B expense guide; GAAP EPS estimates in the wire range from $3.79 (BofA, charge included) to $6.54-$7.54 (charge excluded), so headline 'EPS miss' prints are likely on aggregator screens.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2-26 $2.4B legal charge plus $1.18B severance made a GAAP EPS miss ($6.18 vs ~$7.2) and the stock fell 7.95%, though the guide was the stated driver. The settlement announcement itself on 2026-08-26 lifted the stock ~4.4% pre-market (overhang removed).
findings.why_not_priced: The charge itself is public for two months and is priced; what may not be is the mechanical headline-EPS reaction in the first minutes because consensus aggregators mix pre- and post-charge estimates. Cash is spread over 10 years, so no path to the multiple; sized as a fraction.
findings.independence: Charge size confirmed in https://www.tradingkey.com/analysis/stocks/us-stocks/262225065-meta-stock-forecast-q3-earnings-legal-charge-capex-694-support-october-20-2026-tradingkey (2026-10-20) and EPS dispersion in the cmsinvestments preview; same underlying Meta statement.

findings.finding: The same settlement imposes a 2-hour cumulative daily limit on Facebook+Instagram for under-18s, a midnight-6am night mode and an 8am-3pm school mode in participating states, pending judicial approval with no effective date; any engagement or Q4/2027 revenue commentary on it lands tonight.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print on this line; the August settlement day was positive (+4.4% pre-market), so the market has so far treated the restrictions as small.
findings.why_not_priced: No company quantification exists; if the market thought teen limits material, the August reaction would not have been positive. Teen users are a small share of ad revenue, so the residual is small and one-directional.
findings.independence: Shares the settlement document with the legal-charge finding (one document, two lines: the accrual and the product restriction). Restrictions also described at https://6abc.com/post/meta-settles-states-landmark-social-media-addiction-trial/19738688/.

findings.finding: Q3-26 is the first print since the Muse AI agent launched on 2026-09-08 (US/Canada, free plus $20/$100 monthly tiers): third-party trackers put it at >5M downloads by 2026-09-30 and ~557k-642k US DAU mid-September, but 14-day retention ~22% (Sensor Tower via secondary reports; Morgan Stanley ~20%), and Amazon blocked Muse from Amazon.com on 2026-09-20.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Muse launch drove a ~27% September run (cmsinvestments preview); no prior print carried a Muse disclosure.
findings.source_date: 2026-10 (page date not in URL; content covers late-Sept data)
findings.why_not_priced: Only third-party estimates exist; a first company-reported user or subscriber number tonight would replace them. Revenue contribution in Q3 is immaterial, so this matters only through the narrative supporting the 2027 spend; the retention data and Amazon block cut against a large positive.
findings.independence: Download counts at https://gulfnews.com/technology/companies/metas-new-ai-agent-hits-28-million-downloads-in-just-12-days-1.500684161; Amazon block at https://www.retailgazette.co.uk/blog/2026/09/amazon-blocks-metas-new-ai-shopping-agent-from-its-website/ (2026-09).

findings.finding: The AI-infrastructure credit scare of 2026-10-14/15 (CoreWeave -15% then >25% on the week, CDS >1,000bp; Oracle ~-9%; Nebius ~-25%) touches Meta directly: Meta has committed ~$47B to CoreWeave and Nebius plus a $15B conditional backstop at Nebius, and has used off-balance-sheet JV financing (BlackRock $12.3B El Paso deal, July 2026), so the call will be asked about counterparty and financing exposure.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print turned on counterparty exposure; Meta's own late-2025 $30B bond deal coincided with the -11.3% Q3-25 reaction but the stated driver was expense guidance.
findings.why_not_priced: Financing question answered: the commitments buy compute capacity for Meta's own demand, not to fund distress, and Meta held $90.3B cash vs $83.7B LTD at Q2; so this is a narrative/credit-contagion risk, not a balance-sheet problem. Partly priced in the -4.8% 20-day drift; sized small as a proxy.
findings.independence: Exposure figures from https://cmsinvestments.substack.com/p/meta-q3-preview-the-2027-capex-number (shares a document with the capex finding); El Paso financing at https://api.advisorperspectives.com/articles/2026/07/24/blackrock-12-3-billion-bond-sale-meta-data-center.

findings.finding: Positioning into the print is de-risked rather than crowded long: stock -3.98% over 5 sessions and -4.82% over 20 to $708.2, 8.9% under its 52-week high, underperforming a rising Nasdaq on 2026-10-19 on reported defensive positioning/profit-taking; 25-delta skew -2.0 (calls slightly rich), put/call OI 0.79, short interest ~1.3% of float.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The two most recent prints (-8.0%, -8.6%) came after the stock had not pulled back beforehand per previews; the Jan-26 +10.4% followed a weak run-in. Evidence is anecdotal.
findings.why_not_priced: This is the price itself, so by construction partly priced; filed because a lighter book into the print dampens the downside on a merely in-line 2027 framing. The skew does not lean to puts, so the option market is not paying up for a disappointment.
findings.independence: Run-up and skew from the sealed baseline; short interest from https://equibles.com/stocks/meta/shortinterest.

findings.finding: FX moved roughly as Meta assumed: the dollar index finished Q3-26 about +0.2% (July open to 30 Sept), EUR/USD -0.3%, yen +3.2% vs USD, consistent with the ~1% FX headwind built into the $61-64B guide at July rates, so no FX surprise in the reported quarter.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: FX has not been a driver in the baseline's prints.
findings.why_not_priced: Nothing to price; filed as a checked neutral. Single broker source for quarter-end levels.

outside_window.finding: Court approval and effective date of the teen usage limits under the AG settlement are not yet set; the revenue effect, if any, lands in later quarters.

Sealed baseline straddle is 6.74% (event-implied 6.3%) and another preview cites ~7.3%; the 12% figure is inconsistent with the chain.

baseline_tension: The mild negative lean cuts slightly against a call-leaning skew (-2) and a balanced priced lean, and agrees with the -4.8% 20-day drift and the name's recent habit of selling prints on forward spend; it is not strong enough to argue the options market is wrong, so p_up sits only 5 points under 50.
lessons_applied: Rule 6 (verify the bar): the 2027 capex consensus (~$193B) has one source and BofA/Evercore disagree with it, so the 2027-spend guidance finding was capped from -2.0 to -1.5.

Rule 4 (financing is a question): asked what the CoreWeave/Nebius commitments and JV financings buy - Meta's own compute capacity, with $90.3B cash vs $83.7B LTD - so the credit-contagion finding was cut from -0.5 to -0.3 and kept as a proxy.

Rule 1 (fact is not a reaction) and rule 2 (one-offs): already reflected in the draft (revenue-beat finding at +0.5 given beats sold on 3 of 4 prints; legal accrual at -0.3 as a fraction); left standing.
Rule 7 (positioning): short interest checked (~1.3% of float, not crowded); no change.
